extracted.intended_audience: Navy analysts/managers and graduate-level researchers conducting OMB Circular A-76 cost comparisons (HRMIN managers, NPRDC staff)
extracted.subtask_short: OMB A-76 cost comparison for HRMIN
extracted.subtask_description: Perform an economic cost comparison of in-house versus contract-out performance for the Human Resource Management Information Network (HRMIN) following the framework in OMB Circular No. A-76, including benchmarking, adjustment of vendor charges to in-house usage, and optional present-value analysis. Also documents HRM survey database processing and administration procedures used as inputs to the analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use OMB Circular No. A-76 cost comparison framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the cost comparison framework specified in OMB Circular No. A-76 (5 April 1979) when comparing in-house performance to contract-out alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The thesis explicitly uses A-76 as the framework for analysis; follow its procedures and assumptions when preparing the comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Low-bid rule for contract comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB Circular No. A-76 requires the 'low bid' be used when conducting a cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the basic contract price (low bid) exceeds total in-house costs, it can be assumed in-house performance is less costly and the portions of the comparison dealing with the cost of contracting-out need not be completed (except for specified exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stopping rule and exceptions (taxes/disposal)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the basic contract price exceeds total in-house costs, you may stop the contracting-out cost analysis; the only exception is potential federal income taxes and proceeds from disposal of assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether tax effects or proceeds from asset disposal could alter the conclusion before stopping. The thesis notes a 2% IRS tax rate for the company and assumes assets incorporated in GSA sharing so proceeds are not expected to change the outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include contract administration cost in contract price
rubrics_metrics.description: Add the cost of administering the contract (assumed 4%) to the basic contract price when comparing to in-house costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including this administrative surcharge amplifies the effect where in-house is favored; always include standard contract administration percentages in comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare scope: operating costs only
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit the primary analysis to operating costs; explicitly state exclusions such as service life, benefits, salvage value, and other non-operating considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The thesis examines only operating costs and warns that other considerations (service life, benefits, salvage value) are ignored and could be examined by other methods if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postulate representative in-house usage profile
rubrics_metrics.description: Base adjustments to vendor benchmarked charges on a postulated 'real' in-house usage profile derived from available user data (e.g., connect time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use representative observed user data to estimate 'real' in-house connect time; document assumptions (e.g., working days, yearly hours) and justify representativeness. Sensitivity of final costs to this postulation should be acknowledged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustment factor calculation for benchmarked vendor charges
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust vendor benchmark connect-time/processing charges by computing an adjustment factor = (vendor benchmark hours derived from vendor cost / assumed vendor hourly rate) ÷ postulated in-house hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Tymshare benchmark cost $219,120 ÷ $16/hour = 13,695 benchmark hours; divided by postulated in-house 4,740 hours yields an adjustment factor of 2.9. Choosing the hourly rate and in-house hours materially affects the factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of vendor hourly rate and conservative/worst-case assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Selecting a maximum/peak vendor hourly rate (e.g., $16/hour) produces a 'worst case' benchmark hours value and thus the smallest adjustment factor, leading to the largest reductions in vendor charges when adjusted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about whether rates used are maximum/peak; explain how conservative (worst-case) assumptions affect the adjustment factor and resulting cost comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assume benchmark applicability across vendors only if justified
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply an adjustment factor derived from one vendor's benchmark to another vendor only if an assumption of comparable rates/services is justified (e.g., assuming Boeing Mainstream EKS service rate is same as Tymshare's).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State any cross-vendor rate equivalence assumptions and the rationale; sensitivity to this assumption should be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Present Value (PV) analysis when multi-year comparisons needed
rubrics_metrics.description: When simple inspection is insufficient, use Present Value analysis to compare alternatives on a common time-and-cost basis by discounting future cash flows to present value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PV analysis requires choosing a discount rate (the thesis uses 10%, representing opportunity cost), a time horizon (example: equal five-year useful life for alternatives), and identification of material cost elements. Consult standard references (Horngren 1977; Naval Data Automation Command 1980) for techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of discount rate for government projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that the discount/return rate used (e.g., 10%) reflects the opportunity cost of transferring resources from the private to the public sector, not the government's ability to invest funds to earn returns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document why the chosen discount rate is appropriate for public-sector cost comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define which cost elements are material to PV analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify material cost elements to include in the PV computation (the thesis treats variable tangible costs as material) and state which offsets or intangibles are immaterial (e.g., 2% income tax offset small; cost of capital and insurance deemed too small).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly list included and excluded cost elements and justify exclusions based on materiality to the outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: State multi-year cost assumptions (useful life, recurrence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume recurrence of variable tangible costs for each year of the chosen useful life and choose an equal useful life for alternatives when comparing (example: five-year life assumed for both alternatives).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If service-company 'immortal' assumptions are ignored, state that and explain how it affects the comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: HRM Survey raw-data processing and index computation standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Process HRM Survey raw data by converting tapes to final form through programs that perform editing, consistency checks, creation of unit records from header records, creation of survey records from respondent records, and computation of selected indices (28 indices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document the data-processing pipeline, types of raw records (two header records per unit + respondent records), the indices computed, and any editing/consistency rules used.

rubrics_metrics.name: HRM Database retention and access policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain the HRM Database with the most recent three years of survey data online; remove older data to tape archive and require written special-request approval to access archived data from NPRDC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State retention period (3 years), archival medium (tape), and the procedure for accessing archived data (written request to NPRDC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey administration procedure and CO options
rubrics_metrics.description: During an initial visit by HRM Specialists, the Commanding Officer may (a) decide no further HRM services are needed (survey not given), (b) elect to participate (survey administered and answer sheets sent to NARDAC for scanning and processing), followed by a briefing on results and areas of concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe administrative steps, responsibilities (HRM Specialists, NARDAC, NPRDC), and follow-up (briefing to CO).
